observation.visible_scene: Outdoors in bright daylight, a person's two hands hold a frosted translucent plastic water bottle (blue-and-gold 'PURELO' label) tilted above a small silver two-handled bowl packed with a mound of ice cubes. The bowl rests on a flat-topped grey stone pedestal, with sunlit green foliage and a few white flowers filling the background.
visible_changes: For the first portion (frames 1-13) the bottle is held at a tilt but no outflow is visible; the tilt angle gradually increases, pointing the mouth more downward toward the bowl.
Around frame 14 a thin thread of clear liquid first appears at the bottle's mouth.
Through frames 15-26 a narrow, somewhat intermittent stream falls from the mouth onto the ice.
From frame 27 onward the stream becomes thicker and continuous, pouring onto the center of the ice mound.

The ice mound's silhouette changes over the clip: it starts as a rounded heap and develops a taller, pointed peak at the point where the stream lands, with its surface looking wetter and more translucent.
The holding hands shift slightly and the bottle is progressively tilted further down as pouring continues.
The bowl, pedestal, and background remain fixed in frame position, indicating a stationary camera rather than scene movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether pouring had begun before frame 1 or continues after frame 41 (both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries).
The cause or mechanism of the changing ice-mound shape (water accumulation, melting, or freezing is not determinable from the frames).
The bottle's remaining liquid level and whether it noticeably drops.
What happens after the excerpt ends.
uncertain_details: The exact nature of the mound's peak change (added water vs. rearranged ice) cannot be confirmed.
Minor hand/bottle repositioning is visible but the precise grip adjustment is partly occluded.
The bottle appears frosted/cold; internal liquid level is hard to read through the frosted plastic.
